::: {.lead}
Today there are no new ideas. You use what Lecture 8 taught (matrices, adding
and scaling them, a matrix times a vector and times a matrix, the order of a
product and the inverse) on game problems. Do each activity alone. The
results of the activities are at the end of this worksheet: try first, then
compare.
:::

## Recall

- A matrix has the size rows × columns; the entry a~ij~ is in row i,
  column j.
- Matrices of the same size are added entry by entry; k × A multiplies every
  entry by k.
- Matrix × vector: each row times the vector gives one coordinate.
- Matrix × matrix: entry (i, j) = row i · column j. In AB**v**, B acts first.
- The identity I changes nothing; the inverse undoes a matrix.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="4 × 2|(4, 1)"}
What is the size of a matrix with 2 rows and 4 columns?
:   2 × 4

    Why: rows first, then columns.

The rows (2, 0) and (0, 1) times the vector (3, 5).
:   (6, 5)

    Why: row 1: 2 × 3 + 0 × 5 = 6; row 2: 0 × 3 + 1 × 5 = 5.

In AB**v**, which matrix acts first on **v**?
:   B

    Why: the matrix next to the vector acts first.
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · The enemy table

An RPG keeps its enemies in a matrix E. Row 1 is the slime, row 2 the troll;
the columns are HP, damage and speed:

| | HP | damage | speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| slime (row 1) | 40 | 10 | 4 |
| troll (row 2) | 60 | 20 | 2 |

![Hard mode multiplies every entry of the stats matrix by 1.5.](images/matrix-scale.png){width=80%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Read and change the table · 10 min"}
1. Write the size of E and the entries e~13~ and e~22~. What does each mean?
2. A bat joins the game: HP 20, damage 5, speed 8. Write the new matrix and
   its size.
3. Hard mode is 1.5 × E. Write the hard-mode stats of the troll.

*Your product:* the size, two entries with their meaning, the new matrix
and the troll's hard-mode row.

::: {.check}
E is 2 × 3. e~13~ = 4: the speed of the slime. e~22~ = 20: the damage of the
troll. With the bat as row 3 the matrix is 3 × 3. Hard-mode troll:
1.5 × (60, 20, 2) = (90, 30, 3).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The table"}
E has the rows slime (40, 10, 4) and troll (60, 20, 2); the columns are HP,
damage and speed. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="e~31~|2 × 4"}
Which entry is the HP of the troll?
:   e~21~

    Why: the troll is row 2 and HP is column 1.

What is the size of E with a third enemy?
:   3 × 3

    Why: one more row; the columns stay HP, damage and speed.

What is the slime's damage in hard mode (1.5 × E)?
:   15

    Why: 1.5 × 10 = 15.
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Three enemies at once

Three enemies stand at (2, 1), (5, 3) and (0, 4). The game keeps them as the
columns of one matrix P. In this frame they take the steps (1, 0), (−1, 0)
and (0, −2): the columns of D.

$$P = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad D = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$$

{{< sim file="sims/matrix-lab.html" poster="sims/matrix-lab.png" title="Matrix Lab: add, subtract and multiply by a number" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Move them all · 12 min"}
1. Compute P + D. Where is each enemy now?
2. The next frame has the same steps. Compute P + 2D.
3. Check one column in **Matrix Lab** (enter P and D as A and B).

*Your product:* the two matrices and the three new positions.

::: {.check}
P + D has the rows (3, 4, 0) and (1, 3, 2): the enemies are at (3, 1), (4, 3)
and (0, 2). P + 2D has the rows (4, 3, 0) and (1, 3, 0): (4, 1), (3, 3) and
(0, 0). Each column is a vector addition, done for all enemies at once.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Many at once"}
P has the columns (2, 1), (5, 3), (0, 4); D has the columns (1, 0), (−1, 0),
(0, −2). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(3, 3)|(0, 6)"}
Where is enemy 1 after P + D?
:   (3, 1)

    Why: (2, 1) + (1, 0).

Where is enemy 3 after P + D?
:   (0, 2)

    Why: (0, 4) + (0, −2).

Why can the game add P and D?
:   they have the same size

    Why: both are 2 × 3, so every entry has a partner.
:::
:::

## Activity 3 · Spells on points

A crystal puzzle uses spells. **Stretch** has the rows (2, 0) and (0, 3);
**Turn** has the rows (0, −1) and (1, 0); **Mirror** has the rows (1, 0) and
(0, −1).

![Each row of the matrix times the vector gives one coordinate.](images/matrix-vector.png){width=82%}

{{< sim file="sims/multiply-lab.html" poster="sims/multiply-lab.png" title="Multiply Lab: a 2 × 2 matrix moves a point and a shape" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 3 · Cast and check · 12 min"}
1. On paper, cast Stretch, Turn and Mirror on the point (3, −1). Write both
   rows of each calculation.
2. In **Multiply Lab**, enter each matrix, put P at (3, −1) and compare.
3. Which spell turns the house upside down?

*Your product:* three points with their calculations, and one sentence.

::: {.check}
Stretch: (2 × 3 + 0, 0 + 3 × (−1)) = (6, −3). Turn: (0 + 1, 3 + 0) = (1, 3).
Mirror: (3, 1). Mirror changes the sign of y, so the house is upside down.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Spells"}
Stretch = rows (2, 0), (0, 3); Turn = rows (0, −1), (1, 0); Mirror = rows
(1, 0), (0, −1). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(−3, 1)|(3, −2)"}
Stretch on (1, 2).
:   (2, 6)

    Why: (2 × 1, 3 × 2).

Turn on (4, 2).
:   (−2, 4)

    Why: Turn sends (x, y) to (−y, x).

Mirror on (5, 2).
:   (5, −2)

    Why: Mirror keeps x and changes the sign of y.
:::
:::

## Activity 4 · Which products exist?

Before the game multiplies two matrices, it must check the sizes: AB exists
when A has as many columns as B has rows. (m × **n**) times (**n** × p) gives
m × p.

![Row i of A times column j of B.](images/matrix-matrix.png){width=82%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 4 · Sizes and a product · 12 min"}
1. Does each product exist? If yes, what is its size? (2 × 3)(3 × 4);
   (2 × 2)(2 × 1); (2 × 3)(2 × 3); (3 × 1)(1 × 3).
2. A has the rows (2, 1) and (0, 3); B has the rows (1, 0) and (4, 2).
   Compute AB, writing each entry as a dot product.

*Your product:* four answers about sizes and the matrix AB.

::: {.check}
2 × 4; 2 × 1; no (3 and 2 differ); 3 × 3. AB: row 1 · column 1 = 2 × 1 + 1 × 4
= 6; row 1 · column 2 = 2 × 0 + 1 × 2 = 2; row 2 · column 1 = 0 + 3 × 4 = 12;
row 2 · column 2 = 0 + 3 × 2 = 6. AB has the rows (6, 2) and (12, 6).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Products"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="2 × 3|no product"}
(3 × 2) times (2 × 4). The size?
:   3 × 4

    Why: the inner 2s match; the outer numbers give the size.

(2 × 3) times (2 × 3). The size?
:   it does not exist

    Why: A has 3 columns but B has 2 rows.

A = rows (2, 1), (0, 3); B = rows (1, 0), (4, 2). Row 1 of AB?
:   (6, 2)

    Why: (2, 1) · (1, 4) = 6 and (2, 1) · (0, 2) = 2.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note .ai-task title="Task with AI · A spell on a whole sprite"}
**Goal:** a spreadsheet that applies a spell matrix to all 8 corner points of
a sprite at once and draws the sprite before and after. By hand that is 16
dot products; with an AI assistant it takes a few minutes.

1. **Do it yourself:** draw a small sprite (an arrow, a house) on squared
   paper with 8 corner points and write their coordinates.
2. **Ask the AI:** start with this prompt and add your points.

   ::: {.prompt}
   I have a 2 × 2 matrix with the rows (a, b) and (c, d) in the cells B1, C1,
   B2, C2 of a spreadsheet, and 8 points (x, y) in the columns E and F, rows
   1 to 8. Write the formulas for the new points (ax + by, cx + dy) in the
   columns G and H, and tell me how to draw both sets of points as a scatter
   chart. My points are:
   :::

3. **Check:** put Turn (rows (0, −1) and (1, 0)) in the matrix cells. Work out
   two of the new points by hand and compare with the sheet. Then try Stretch
   and Mirror.

*Your product:* the sheet with its chart, your two hand checks, and one
sentence on what you had to correct (or "nothing").

::: {.check}
A good sheet: with Turn, every point (x, y) becomes (−y, x), and the chart
shows the sprite turned by 90° anticlockwise around the origin; with the
identity (rows (1, 0), (0, 1)) nothing moves. AI formulas often mix up the
cells b and c (using cx + by): check one point where x and y are different,
for example (2, 1) → (−1, 2) with Turn.
:::
:::

## Activity 5 · One spell from two

The game casts Grow (rows (2, 0), (0, 2)) and Turn (rows (0, −1), (1, 0)) on
every point of a model. It multiplies the two matrices once and uses the
result for every point. Flip has the rows (−1, 0) and (0, 1).

![Stretch then turn, and turn then stretch, give different shapes.](images/order-matters.png){width=82%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 5 · Combine and compare · 12 min"}
1. Compute Grow × Turn. Check it on (1, 0).
2. Take the point (4, −1). Apply Flip then Turn, and Turn then Flip.
3. Which spell undoes Grow × Turn? Describe it in words.

*Your product:* the matrix Grow × Turn, two end points, and one sentence.

::: {.check}
Grow × Turn has the rows (0, −2) and (2, 0); on (1, 0) it gives (0, 2): turned
by 90° and twice as far. Flip then Turn: (4, −1) → (−4, −1) → (1, −4). Turn
then Flip: (4, −1) → (1, 4) → (−1, 4). To undo Grow × Turn, turn back by 90°
(clockwise) and halve the distance.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Two spells"}
Grow = rows (2, 0), (0, 2); Turn = rows (0, −1), (1, 0); Flip = rows
(−1, 0), (0, 1). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(4, 1)|rows (2, 0) and (0, −2)"}
Grow × Turn as one matrix.
:   rows (0, −2) and (2, 0)

    Why: row (2, 0) · the columns (0, 1) and (−1, 0) gives 0 and −2; row (0, 2) gives 2 and 0.

From (4, −1), Flip then Turn.
:   (1, −4)

    Why: Flip: (−4, −1); Turn: (−y, x) = (1, −4).

From (4, −1), Turn then Flip.
:   (−1, 4)

    Why: Turn: (1, 4); Flip: (−1, 4).
:::
:::

## Case study: Crystal Spells

*Crystal Spells* is a made-up puzzle game. The crystal starts at (2, 1). Each
spell is a 2 × 2 matrix: **Grow** = rows (2, 0), (0, 2); **Shrink** = rows
(0.5, 0), (0, 0.5); **Turn** = rows (0, −1), (1, 0); **Flip** = rows (−1, 0),
(0, 1); **Stay** = the identity. The Game challenge of the interactive page
asks harder puzzles with these spells: two spells in a row, a spell cast
twice, and the spell that undoes another.

{{< sim file="sims/crystal-spells.html" poster="sims/crystal-spells.png" title="Crystal Spells: cast the right matrix" kind="game" height="720" >}}

## Exercises

1. The enemy table has the rows (40, 10, 4) and (60, 20, 2). Write 2 × the
   table.
2. Two coins at (1, 3) and (4, 0) fall by 2 units. Write the position matrix,
   the step matrix and their sum.
3. Stretch = rows (2, 0), (0, 3). Where does it send (−1, 2)?
4. Does (1 × 2)(2 × 3) exist? What is its size?
5. Compute AB for A = rows (1, 0), (2, 1) and B = rows (3, 1), (0, 2).
6. From (1, 3), cast Turn, then Flip. Where does the point land?
7. Which spell undoes Shrink?
8. Why does Turn × Flip differ from Flip × Turn? Check on (1, 0).

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. Rows (80, 20, 8) and (120, 40, 4).
2. Columns (1, 3) and (4, 0), plus columns (0, −2) and (0, −2): columns (1, 1) and (4, −2).
3. (−2, 6).
4. Yes, 1 × 3.
5. Rows (3, 1) and (6, 4).
6. Turn: (−3, 1); Flip: (3, 1).
7. Grow.
8. On (1, 0): Flip then Turn gives (0, −1); Turn then Flip gives (0, 1). The order matters.
:::
